1 Setup

Code 
# Force UTF-8 so unicode (mL/min/1.73m², ±, ≥) renders correctly.
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_ALL", "en_US.UTF-8"))

# Lightweight install guard so the project renders on a fresh machine.
.need <- c("readxl","dplyr","tidyr","purrr","tibble","flextable","officer","ggplot2","rvg")
.miss <- setdiff(.need, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(.miss)) install.packages(.miss, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
# bodycompref is GitHub-only (p-mq/bodycompref); supplies the muscle Z-score.
if (!requireNamespace("bodycompref", quietly = TRUE)) {
  if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  remotes::install_github("p-mq/bodycompref")
}

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(flextable)
library(ggplot2)

# Output directory for downloadable Word copies of every table.
docx_dir <- "docs/tables/heatmap"
dir.create(docx_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Absolute path: flextable_to_rmd() can change the working directory mid-render,
# which would break later saves to a relative docx_dir.
docx_dir <- normalizePath(docx_dir, mustWork = TRUE)

save_ft_docx <- function(ft, name) {
  flextable::save_as_docx(ft, path = file.path(docx_dir, paste0(name, ".docx")))
  invisible(ft)
}

# Output directory for downloadable PowerPoint copies of the plot panels.
ppt_dir <- "docs/ppt"
dir.create(ppt_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Absolute path for the same reason as docx_dir (cwd can change mid-render).
ppt_dir <- normalizePath(ppt_dir, mustWork = TRUE)

# Render a list of ggplots inline AND write them to an editable .pptx (one slide
# per plot) under docs/ppt/, then print a Markdown download link. Must be called
# inside a `results: asis` chunk. Editable vector via rvg::dml; raster fallback.
emit_plots <- function(plots, fname,
                       label = "⬇️ Download these panels as PowerPoint (editable)") {
  for (p in plots) print(p)                                   # figures, inline
  loc <- officer::ph_location(left = 0.5, top = 1.2, width = 9, height = 5.14)  # 7:4
  doc <- officer::read_pptx()
  for (p in plots) {
    doc <- officer::add_slide(doc, layout = "Title and Content", master = "Office Theme")
    gr  <- tryCatch(rvg::dml(ggobj = p), error = function(e) NULL)
    doc <- officer::ph_with(doc, if (is.null(gr)) p else gr, location = loc)
  }
  print(doc, target = file.path(ppt_dir, paste0(fname, ".pptx")))
  cat(sprintf("\n\n[%s](../ppt/%s.pptx)\n\n", label, fname))
}

# --- Two colouring schemes -------------------------------------------------
# V1: 4-level categorical severity.  <5 yellow · 5–10 orange · 10–20 red · >20 purple.
cat4_fill <- function(x) {
  dplyr::case_when(is.na(x) ~ "#FFFFFF",
                   x <  5  ~ "#FFEDA0",   # yellow
                   x < 10  ~ "#FEB24C",   # orange
                   x <= 20 ~ "#F03B20",   # red
                   TRUE    ~ "#6A51A3")   # purple
}

# V2: continuous gradient across `stops` (low 0 % -> high), saturating at `dom` %.
# (base grDevices, no extra dependency). The exact % is printed in every cell.
ramp_fill <- function(x, stops, dom = 30) {
  f   <- grDevices::colorRamp(stops)
  x2  <- pmin(pmax(x, 0), dom) / dom
  out <- rep("#FFFFFF", length(x))      # NA -> white (no data)
  ok  <- !is.na(x2)
  if (any(ok)) {
    m <- f(x2[ok])
    out[ok] <- grDevices::rgb(m[, 1], m[, 2], m[, 3], maxColorValue = 255)
  }
  out
}
# Yellow -> orange -> red ramp for Part B (low % = yellow, high % = deep red).
CONT_STOPS <- c("#FFEDA0", "#FEB24C", "#F03B20", "#B2182B")

2 Data Management

All variables used in this report are created in the code chunk below (click ▸ Code to expand). Every other section’s code is likewise available under its own ▸ Code button.

Code 
raw <- suppressWarnings(
  readxl::read_excel("Data/OncoGFR1200_MGH_chemo_CJASN.xlsx")
)

# Cancer-site labels for `site.ajcc` (codes 1-11; the 11 groups of the
# manuscript Table 1). The source file ships no codebook for them. Four are
# fixed by the sex distribution and are safe:
#   6  = Breast                      (272 patients, 98.9 % female)
#   7  = Female reproductive organs  ( 60 patients,  100 % female)
#   11 = Male genital organs         (262 patients,    0 % female)
#   9  = Endocrine system            ( 39 patients, 84.6 % female - thyroid)
# The other seven cannot be told apart from the data alone, so they print as
# their code until the mapping is supplied. Fill them in here and nothing
# else needs to change.
SITE_LABS <- c(
  "1"  = "Site 1",
  "2"  = "Site 2",
  "3"  = "Site 3",
  "4"  = "Site 4",
  "5"  = "Site 5",
  "6"  = "Breast",
  "7"  = "Female reproductive organs",
  "8"  = "Site 8",
  "9"  = "Endocrine system",
  "10" = "Site 10",
  "11" = "Male genital organs")
dat <- raw %>%
  dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("...70", "...75"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    sex     = factor(gender, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    bmi_grp = cut(BMI, breaks = c(-Inf, 20, 25, 30, Inf), right = FALSE,
                  labels = c("<20", "20 to <25", "25 to <30", ">=30")),
    # metastasis is complete (0/1) in this dataset — no "Unknown" level.
    met_grp = factor(metastasis, levels = c(0, 1),
                     labels = c("Not metastatic", "Metastatic")),
    age_grp = factor(ifelse(age >= 70, ">=70", "<70"), levels = c("<70", ">=70")),
    age65 = age >= 65,
    # WHO BMI bands, for Table 1 only. Deliberately NOT bmi_grp, whose
    # <20 / 20-25 / 25-30 / >=30 cuts are the ones the heatmap subgroup
    # columns use and are matched by string in several lookups.
    bmi_who = cut(BMI, breaks = c(-Inf, 18.5, 25, 30, Inf), right = FALSE,
                  labels = c("Underweight (<18.5 kg/m\u00b2)",
                             "Normal range (18.5-24.9 kg/m\u00b2)",
                             "Overweight (25-29.9 kg/m\u00b2)",
                             "Obese (\u226530 kg/m\u00b2)")),
    # Smoking is NOT coded in the intuitive order. Checked against the file's
    # own never./former./current.smoker indicator columns: 0 = never (604),
    # 1 = CURRENT (128), 2 = FORMER (468). Levels are then set to the
    # never/former/current reading order.
    smoke_grp = factor(c("Never", "Current", "Former")[match(Smoking, c(0, 1, 2))],
                       levels = c("Never", "Former", "Current")),
    # stage 5 has stageV = 1 for all 55 of its patients (and TIS for 43 of
    # them), i.e. the unstageable band the template calls "Not applicable".
    stage_grp = factor(stage, levels = 1:5,
                       labels = c("1", "2", "3", "4", "Not applicable")),
    # Cancer site: site.ajcc has exactly the 11 groups the template lists.
    # SITE_LABS (above) holds the code -> label mapping.
    site_grp = factor(site.ajcc, levels = 1:11, labels = SITE_LABS),
    # ECOG performance status; only 8 patients are ECOG 3, so lump 2+3 -> "≥2".
    ecog_grp = factor(ifelse(ecog >= 2, "≥2", as.character(ecog)), levels = c("0", "1", "≥2")),
    # LOESS x-axes: eGFRcys (CKD-EPI 2012) vs eGFRcr (CKD-EPI 2021). The RATIO is
    # scale-invariant; the DIFFERENCE is not, so it is taken on the indexed scale
    # (mL/min/1.73 m²). Both use the index columns.
    egfr_ratio = CKDEPIcysindex / CKDEPIcr21index,
    egfr_diff  = CKDEPIcysindex - CKDEPIcr21index,
    # % difference (Cys − Cr) relative to creatinine; scale-invariant.
    egfr_pctdiff = (CKDEPIcysindex - CKDEPIcr21index) / CKDEPIcr21index * 100,
    # Section 14 sensitivity definition: the same discordance measured against
    # Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance, both terms on the ACTUAL-BSA
    # (non-indexed) scale. This is the index the grant page plots.
    egfr_pctdiff_cg = (CKDEPIcrcys21non_index - CGnon_index) / CGnon_index * 100
  )

# Body-composition subset (465 patients, matched on `protocol`). Adds a Prado
# sarcopenia group and an in_bodycomp flag; NA for the other 735 patients.
.bc <- suppressWarnings(readxl::read_excel("Data/OncoGFR_MGH_final_0428.xlsx"))

# Muscle Z-score is RECOMPUTED here with the bodycompref package (L3 skeletal
# muscle index vs the Framingham reference; Tonnesen 2023) rather than reusing the
# file's stored `z_score`, which came from an older build whose age floor was 35.
# The current reference window is 38-80, so age is clamped into it (<38 -> 38,
# >80 -> 80). The cohort spans 19-86 y, so 58 of 465 sit outside that window and
# are anchored to a boundary age -- flagged in the Muscle Z-score section.
.bc_age <- pmin(pmax(as.integer(round(as.numeric(.bc$age))), 38L), 80L)
.bc_ok  <- !is.na(.bc_age) & !is.na(.bc$SMI) & .bc$sex %in% c("Female", "Male")
.bc$muscle_z_ref <- NA_real_
.bc$muscle_z_ref[.bc_ok] <- bodycompref::reference_z_scores(
  rep("SMI", sum(.bc_ok)), as.character(.bc$sex)[.bc_ok], rep("L3", sum(.bc_ok)),
  .bc_age[.bc_ok], as.numeric(.bc$SMI)[.bc_ok])

dat <- dat %>% dplyr::mutate(
  in_bodycomp = protocol %in% .bc$protocol,
  sarc_grp = factor(.bc$sarcopenia_prado[match(protocol, .bc$protocol)],
                    levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Non-sarcopenic", "Sarcopenic")),
  muscle_z = .bc$muscle_z_ref[match(protocol, .bc$protocol)]  # bodycompref L3 SMI Z
)

# Fried frailty class (separate file; key is misspelled 'protocal'); 592 of 1200 have it.
.fr <- suppressWarnings(readxl::read_excel("Data/Frailty data to MGH.xlsx"))
# 0/1/2 carry no codebook in the source file; the ordering was verified against
# external markers (mean age 67.4 -> 69.4 -> 70.9, trend p = 6e-05; ECOG >=2
# 0.0% -> 5.4% -> 27.4%, p = 2e-27), confirming the standard Fried ordering.
dat$fried_grp <- factor(.fr$fried_classification[match(dat$protocol, .fr$protocal)],
                        levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                        labels = c("Non-frail", "Pre-frail", "Frail"))

# Nutrition markers (separate file; key = 'Protocol Number'); 689 of 1200 have them.
# Cachexia (0 = No, 1 = Yes) and ASG-PPP / PG-SGA global rating (coded 1/2 — confirm mapping).
.nut <- suppressWarnings(readxl::read_excel("Data/Nutrition data.xlsx"))
names(.nut) <- trimws(names(.nut))
.nut_key <- match(dat$protocol, .nut$`Protocol Number`)
dat$cachexia_grp <- factor(.nut$Cachexia[.nut_key], levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
dat$asgppp_grp   <- factor(.nut$`ASG-PPP`[.nut_key], levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("1", "2"))

# --- Equation registry: type + label + index/non-index columns -------------
# Reference = measured GFR. Note: the creatinine CKD-EPI column is the 2021
# (race-free) equation; the hyphen in "EKFCcrcysnon-index" is intentional.
reg <- tibble::tribble(
  ~equation,       ~type,        ~label,             ~index_col,           ~nonindex_col,
  "CKDEPIcr21",    "eGFRcr",     "CKD-EPI 2021",     "CKDEPIcr21index",    "CKDEPIcr21non_index",
  "EKFCcr",        "eGFRcr",     "EKFC 2021",        "EKFCcrindex",        "EKFCcrnon_index",
  "CKDEPIcys",     "eGFRcys",    "CKD-EPI 2012",     "CKDEPIcysindex",     "CKDEPIcysnon_index",
  "EKFCcys",       "eGFRcys",    "EKFC 2023",        "EKFCcysindex",       "EKFCcysnon_index",
  "CKDEPIcrcys21", "eGFRcr-cys", "CKD-EPI 2021",     "CKDEPIcrcys21index", "CKDEPIcrcys21non_index",
  "EKFCcrcys",     "eGFRcr-cys", "EKFC 2023",        "EKFCcrcysindex",     "EKFCcrcysnon-index",
  "CG",            "ClCr",       "Cockcroft-Gault",  "CGindex",            "CGnon_index",
  "CKDEPI4mark",   "Panel",      "CKD-EPI 4-marker", "CKDEPI4mark",        "CKDEPI4marknon_index"
)
MGFR <- c(index = "mGFRindex", nonindex = "mGFRnon_index")

# --- Dosing rules ----------------------------------------------------------
dose_tier <- function(gfr, drug) {           # higher integer = more drug; 0 = avoid
  drug <- tolower(drug)
  if (drug == "cisplatin")
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr >= 60 ~ 3, gfr >= 50 ~ 2, gfr >= 40 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  else if (drug == "methotrexate")   # ADDIKD: ≥60 full(3); 45-<60 −25%(2); 30-<45 −50%(1); <30 avoid(0)
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr >= 60 ~ 3, gfr >= 45 ~ 2, gfr >= 30 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  else if (drug == "melphalan")
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr > 60 ~ 2, gfr >= 30 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  else stop("unknown drug: ", drug)
}
dose_class_tier <- function(gfr, mgfr, drug) {
  te <- dose_tier(gfr, drug); tr <- dose_tier(mgfr, drug)
  dplyr::case_when(is.na(te) | is.na(tr) ~ NA_character_,
                   te > tr ~ "Overdose", te < tr ~ "Underdose", TRUE ~ "Concordant")
}
# Carboplatin Calvert (AUC 5): over if 5*(eGFR+25) > k_hi*(mGFR+25); under if < k_lo.
# ±20% → k_hi=6, k_lo=4   |   ±15% → k_hi=5.75, k_lo=4.25
carbo_class <- function(gfr, mgfr, k_hi = 6, k_lo = 4) {
  pred <- 5 * (gfr + 25)
  dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) | is.na(mgfr) ~ NA_character_,
                   pred > k_hi * (mgfr + 25) ~ "Overdose",
                   pred < k_lo * (mgfr + 25) ~ "Underdose", TRUE ~ "Concordant")
}

TIER_DRUGS  <- c("cisplatin", "methotrexate", "melphalan")
CARBO_BANDS <- list(carboplatin_b20 = c(k_hi = 6, k_lo = 4),
                    carboplatin_b15 = c(k_hi = 5.75, k_lo = 4.25))

# Patient-level classification (carries subgroup columns) for one GFR scale.
# `data` lets a subset (e.g. the 465 body-comp cohort) reuse the same logic.
build_class_long <- function(scale = c("index", "nonindex"), data = dat) {
  scale  <- match.arg(scale)
  col_of <- function(eq) {
    r <- reg[reg$equation == eq, ]
    if (scale == "index") r$index_col[[1]] else r$nonindex_col[[1]]
  }
  mgfr <- data[[MGFR[[scale]]]]
  base <- dplyr::select(data, sex, bmi_grp, met_grp, age_grp, ecog_grp, fried_grp,
                        egfr_ratio, egfr_diff, egfr_pctdiff, egfr_pctdiff_cg,
                        sarc_grp, muscle_z,
                        cachexia_grp, asgppp_grp)
  base$mgfr_x <- mgfr   # scale-appropriate measured GFR, for the mGFR-on-x LOESS set
  tier <- purrr::map_dfr(reg$equation, function(eq) {
    g <- data[[col_of(eq)]]
    purrr::map_dfr(TIER_DRUGS, function(dr)
      dplyr::bind_cols(base, tibble::tibble(equation = eq, drug = dr,
                                            cls = dose_class_tier(g, mgfr, dr))))
  })
  carbo <- purrr::map_dfr(reg$equation, function(eq) {
    g <- data[[col_of(eq)]]
    purrr::map_dfr(names(CARBO_BANDS), function(bn) {
      k <- CARBO_BANDS[[bn]]
      dplyr::bind_cols(base, tibble::tibble(equation = eq, drug = bn,
                                            cls = carbo_class(g, mgfr, k[["k_hi"]], k[["k_lo"]])))
    })
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(tier, carbo)
}
cl_index    <- build_class_long("index")
cl_nonindex <- build_class_long("nonindex")

# 465-patient body-composition subset (adds the Sarcopenia column group).
dat_465         <- dat %>% dplyr::filter(in_bodycomp)
cl_index_465    <- build_class_long("index",    dat_465)
cl_nonindex_465 <- build_class_long("nonindex", dat_465)

# Internal (syntactic) column keys + their display labels.
SUB_COLS <- c("Overall", "Female", "Male", "bmi1", "bmi2", "bmi3", "bmi4",
              "met_no", "met_yes", "age_lt70", "age_ge70")
SUB_LABS <- c(Overall = "Overall", Female = "Female", Male = "Male",
              bmi1 = "<20", bmi2 = "20 to <25", bmi3 = "25 to <30", bmi4 = ">=30",
              met_no = "Not metastatic", met_yes = "Metastatic",
              age_lt70 = "<70", age_ge70 = "≥70")

# Extended set for the 465 body-comp subset: adds a Sarcopenia (Prado) group.
SUB_COLS_465 <- c(SUB_COLS, "sarc_no", "sarc_yes")
SUB_LABS_465 <- c(SUB_LABS, sarc_no = "Non-sarcopenic", sarc_yes = "Sarcopenic")

# Build the equation × subgroup % table for one drug and direction.
# extra = TRUE appends the Sarcopenia (Prado) columns (465 body-comp subset).
subgroup_table <- function(cl, drug_id, direction, extra = FALSE) {
  s <- cl %>% dplyr::filter(drug == drug_id, !is.na(cls))
  pct <- function(d) if (nrow(d)) round(mean(d$cls == direction) * 100, 1) else NA_real_
  lvl <- function(d, col, value) pct(d[!is.na(d[[col]]) & d[[col]] == value, ])
  per_eq <- function(eq) {
    e <- s %>% dplyr::filter(equation == eq)
    out <- tibble::tibble(
      equation         = eq,
      Overall          = pct(e),
      Female           = lvl(e, "sex", "Female"),
      Male             = lvl(e, "sex", "Male"),
      bmi1    = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", "<20"),
      bmi2    = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", "20 to <25"),
      bmi3    = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", "25 to <30"),
      bmi4    = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", ">=30"),
      met_no   = lvl(e, "met_grp", "Not metastatic"),
      met_yes  = lvl(e, "met_grp", "Metastatic"),
      age_lt70 = lvl(e, "age_grp", "<70"),
      age_ge70 = lvl(e, "age_grp", ">=70")
    )
    if (extra) {
      out$sarc_no  <- lvl(e, "sarc_grp", "Non-sarcopenic")
      out$sarc_yes <- lvl(e, "sarc_grp", "Sarcopenic")
    }
    out
  }
  cols <- if (extra) SUB_COLS_465 else SUB_COLS
  purrr::map_dfr(reg$equation, per_eq) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(reg, equation, type, label), by = "equation") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(type = factor(type, levels = unique(reg$type))) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(type, match(equation, reg$equation)) %>%
    dplyr::select(type, label, dplyr::all_of(cols))
}

# Render one heatmap flextable. `fill_fn(v)` -> per-cell hex; `dark_fn(v)` -> TRUE
# where the fill is dark enough to need white text.
make_tl_ft <- function(tab, title, fill_fn, dark_fn, extra = FALSE) {
  cols  <- if (extra) SUB_COLS_465 else SUB_COLS
  labs  <- if (extra) SUB_LABS_465 else SUB_LABS
  spanv <- c("", "", "", "Sex", "BMI category (kg/m²)", "Metastatic disease", "Age (years)")
  spanw <- c(1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 2, 2)
  if (extra) { spanv <- c(spanv, "Sarcopenia (Prado)"); spanw <- c(spanw, 2) }
  ncol_total <- length(c("type", "label", cols))
  ft <- flextable::flextable(tab, col_keys = c("type", "label", cols))
  ft <- flextable::set_header_labels(ft,
    values = c(list(type = "eGFR type", label = "Equation"), as.list(labs)))
  # Group-spanner header row (Sex / BMI / Metastatic / Age [/ Sarcopenia]).
  ft <- flextable::add_header_row(ft, top = TRUE, values = spanv, colwidths = spanw)
  # Title row across the whole table ("OVERDOSE (%)" / "UNDERDOSE (%)").
  ft <- flextable::add_header_row(ft, top = TRUE, values = title, colwidths = ncol_total)
  for (cc in cols) {
    v  <- tab[[cc]]
    ft <- flextable::bg(ft, j = cc, bg = fill_fn(v), part = "body")
    # white text on dark cells — scalar colour on specific rows (avoids a
    # vectorised colour arg, which is fragile under R 4.4).
    dark <- which(dark_fn(v))
    if (length(dark)) ft <- flextable::color(ft, i = dark, j = cc, color = "white", part = "body")
  }
  ft <- flextable::merge_v(ft, j = "type", part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::valign(ft, j = "type", valign = "top", part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = cols, align = "center", part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, i = 2, align = "center", part = "header")  # spanner row
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, i = 1, align = "left",   part = "header")  # title row
  ft <- flextable::bold(ft, part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, size = 9, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, i = 1, size = 11, part = "header")
  flextable::set_table_properties(ft, layout = "autofit", width = 1)  # renderer-side sizing
}

# Build the flextable for one (cl, drug, direction) under colour scheme `version`.
build_ft <- function(cl, drug_id, direction, version, extra = FALSE) {
  tab   <- subgroup_table(cl, drug_id, direction, extra)
  title <- paste0(toupper(direction), " (%)")
  if (version == "cat") {
    fill_fn <- cat4_fill
    dark_fn <- function(x) !is.na(x) & x >= 10            # red & purple -> white text
  } else {
    fill_fn <- function(x) ramp_fill(x, CONT_STOPS, 30)   # yellow->red, saturate at 30 %
    dark_fn <- function(x) !is.na(x) & x >= 20            # white text on the red end
  }
  make_tl_ft(tab, title, fill_fn, dark_fn, extra)
}

DRUGS <- list(
  list(id = "carboplatin_b20", lab = "Carboplatin (±20%)"),
  list(id = "carboplatin_b15", lab = "Carboplatin (±15%)"),
  list(id = "cisplatin",       lab = "Cisplatin"),
  list(id = "methotrexate",    lab = "Methotrexate"),
  list(id = "melphalan",       lab = "Melphalan")
)
DRUG_IDS  <- vapply(DRUGS, `[[`, "", "id")
DRUG_LABS <- vapply(DRUGS, `[[`, "", "lab")

# ===== FINAL HEATMAP PLOTS =================================================
# Dosing rules transcribed from final_chemos.docx (Dropbox,
# Cystatin_C/Brazil/Dosing_Paper_Leyre/). Tiers are ORDINAL dose levels, higher
# = more drug. NOTE tier 0 no longer always means "avoid": for etoposide it is a
# 50 % dose and for melphalan 140 mg/m². Band edges follow the document; where a
# document band stops at x.99 the next tier starts at x, so no GFR falls in a gap.
dose_tier_final <- function(gfr, drug) {
  d <- tolower(drug)
  if (d == "pemetrexed")          # >=45 full | <45 avoid
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr >= 45 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  else if (d == "etoposide")      # >=50 full | 15-50 -25% | <15 -50%
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr >= 50 ~ 2, gfr >= 15 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  else if (d == "capecitabine")   # >=50 full | 30-50 -25% | <30 avoid
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr >= 50 ~ 2, gfr >= 30 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  else if (d == "bleomycin")      # >=60 full | 46-60 70% | 30-45.99 60% | <30 avoid
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr >= 60 ~ 3, gfr >= 46 ~ 2,
                     gfr >= 30 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  else if (d == "ifosfamide")     # >60 full | 40-60 75% | 20-40 50% | <20 avoid
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr > 60 ~ 3, gfr >= 40 ~ 2,
                     gfr >= 20 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  # >60 full 200 mg/m^2 | <=60 -> 140. The doc's 30-59 and <30 bands both
  # prescribe 140, so they collapse into one tier.
  else if (d == "melphalan")
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr > 60 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  else if (d == "methotrexate")   # >60 full | 45-59.99 -25% | 30-44.99 -50% | <30 avoid
    dplyr::case_when(is.na(gfr) ~ NA_real_, gfr > 60 ~ 3, gfr >= 45 ~ 2,
                     gfr >= 30 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  # Cisplatin is NOT in final_chemos.docx. It keeps this project's existing
  # rule (>=60 full | 50-59 -25% | 40-49 -50% | <40 avoid); delegating to
  # dose_tier() means the Section 15 cisplatin tables and every earlier
  # section on the page can never drift apart.
  else if (d == "cisplatin") dose_tier(gfr, "cisplatin")
  else stop("unknown drug: ", d)
}

FINAL_TIER_DRUGS <- c("pemetrexed", "etoposide", "capecitabine", "bleomycin",
                      "ifosfamide", "melphalan", "methotrexate", "cisplatin")
# Two drugs are not from final_chemos.docx: carboplatin keeps the Calvert band
# rule (it is dosed to a target AUC, not from a threshold table, so it could
# not appear in that document), and cisplatin keeps this project's existing
# tier rule. Both are listed first, ahead of the seven document drugs.
FINAL_DRUGS <- list(
  list(id = "carboplatin_b20", lab = "Carboplatin (±20%)"),
  list(id = "carboplatin_b15", lab = "Carboplatin (±15%)"),
  list(id = "cisplatin",       lab = "Cisplatin"),
  list(id = "pemetrexed",      lab = "Pemetrexed"),
  list(id = "etoposide",       lab = "Etoposide"),
  list(id = "capecitabine",    lab = "Capecitabine"),
  list(id = "bleomycin",       lab = "Bleomycin"),
  list(id = "ifosfamide",      lab = "Ifosfamide"),
  list(id = "melphalan",       lab = "Melphalan"),
  list(id = "methotrexate",    lab = "Methotrexate")
)

# Row order and grouping from the manuscript table: creatinine-based equations
# (incl. Cockcroft-Gault), then cystatin, then combined. CKD-EPI 4-marker is
# deliberately excluded. Black rules close each eGFR-type block.
FINAL_EQS  <- c("CKDEPIcr21", "EKFCcr", "CG", "CKDEPIcys", "EKFCcys",
                "CKDEPIcrcys21", "EKFCcrcys")
FINAL_RULES <- c(3, 5)

FINAL_SUB_COLS <- c("Overall", "Female", "Male", "bmi1", "bmi2", "bmi3", "bmi4",
                    "met_no", "met_yes", "age_lt70", "age_ge70",
                    "sarc_no", "sarc_yes")
# Column N, counted once from the cohort and printed in every header. The two
# sarcopenia columns come from the 465-patient body-composition subset, so they
# sum to 465 and not 1,200 — stated under the section heading.
.final_n <- c(
  Overall  = nrow(dat),
  Female   = sum(dat$sex      == "Female",         na.rm = TRUE),
  Male     = sum(dat$sex      == "Male",           na.rm = TRUE),
  bmi1     = sum(dat$bmi_grp  == "<20",            na.rm = TRUE),
  bmi2     = sum(dat$bmi_grp  == "20 to <25",      na.rm = TRUE),
  bmi3     = sum(dat$bmi_grp  == "25 to <30",      na.rm = TRUE),
  bmi4     = sum(dat$bmi_grp  == ">=30",           na.rm = TRUE),
  met_no   = sum(dat$met_grp  == "Not metastatic", na.rm = TRUE),
  met_yes  = sum(dat$met_grp  == "Metastatic",     na.rm = TRUE),
  age_lt70 = sum(dat$age_grp  == "<70",            na.rm = TRUE),
  age_ge70 = sum(dat$age_grp  == ">=70",           na.rm = TRUE),
  sarc_no  = sum(dat$sarc_grp == "Non-sarcopenic", na.rm = TRUE),
  sarc_yes = sum(dat$sarc_grp == "Sarcopenic",     na.rm = TRUE))
# Non-breaking spaces (U+00A0) so a label never breaks mid-band: the BMI
# categories used to wrap to "20 to" / "<25" in the narrow columns, and
# "Not metastatic" to "Not" / "metastatic". "N = n" is likewise
# unbreakable, and header line spacing in final_ft() puts air between the
# category line and the count.
# "Non-sarcopenic" breaks at the HYPHEN, which U+00A0 cannot stop, so it gets
# word joiners (U+2060) on both sides instead. U+2011 (non-breaking hyphen)
# would be the obvious fix but Arial has no glyph for it, so a Windows reader
# opening the .docx would see tofu; U+2060 is default-ignorable, so the worst
# case there is the old wrap, not a stray box.
.nb <- function(x) gsub(" ", "\u00A0", x, fixed = TRUE)
FINAL_SUB_LABS <- stats::setNames(
  paste0(c("Overall", "Female", "Male",
           "<20", .nb("20 to <25"), .nb("25 to <30"), "≥30",
           .nb("Not metastatic"), "Metastatic", "<70", "≥70",
           "Non\u2060-\u2060sarcopenic", "Sarcopenic"),
         "\nN\u00A0=\u00A0", .final_n[FINAL_SUB_COLS]),
  FINAL_SUB_COLS)

# Patient-level classification under the FINAL rules, for one GFR scale.
build_final_long <- function(scale = c("index", "nonindex"), data = dat) {
  scale  <- match.arg(scale)
  col_of <- function(eq) {
    r <- reg[reg$equation == eq, ]
    if (scale == "index") r$index_col[[1]] else r$nonindex_col[[1]]
  }
  mgfr <- data[[MGFR[[scale]]]]
  base <- dplyr::select(data, sex, bmi_grp, met_grp, age_grp, sarc_grp)
  tier <- purrr::map_dfr(FINAL_EQS, function(eq) {
    g <- data[[col_of(eq)]]
    purrr::map_dfr(FINAL_TIER_DRUGS, function(dr) {
      te <- dose_tier_final(g, dr); tr <- dose_tier_final(mgfr, dr)
      dplyr::bind_cols(base, tibble::tibble(
        equation = eq, drug = dr,
        cls = dplyr::case_when(is.na(te) | is.na(tr) ~ NA_character_,
                               te > tr ~ "Overdose", te < tr ~ "Underdose",
                               TRUE ~ "Concordant")))
    })
  })
  carbo <- purrr::map_dfr(FINAL_EQS, function(eq) {
    g <- data[[col_of(eq)]]
    purrr::map_dfr(names(CARBO_BANDS), function(bn) {
      k <- CARBO_BANDS[[bn]]
      dplyr::bind_cols(base, tibble::tibble(
        equation = eq, drug = bn,
        cls = carbo_class(g, mgfr, k[["k_hi"]], k[["k_lo"]])))
    })
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(tier, carbo)
}
fin_index    <- build_final_long("index")
fin_nonindex <- build_final_long("nonindex")

# % in `direction` for one drug, by equation (FINAL_EQS order) × subgroup.
final_subgroup_table <- function(cl, drug_id, direction) {
  s   <- cl %>% dplyr::filter(drug == drug_id, !is.na(cls))
  pct <- function(d) if (nrow(d)) round(mean(d$cls == direction) * 100, 1) else NA_real_
  lvl <- function(d, col, value) pct(d[!is.na(d[[col]]) & d[[col]] == value, ])
  purrr::map_dfr(FINAL_EQS, function(eq) {
    e <- s %>% dplyr::filter(equation == eq)
    r <- reg[reg$equation == eq, ]
    tibble::tibble(
      type = r$type[[1]], label = r$label[[1]],
      Overall  = pct(e),
      Female   = lvl(e, "sex", "Female"),      Male     = lvl(e, "sex", "Male"),
      bmi1     = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", "<20"),     bmi2     = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", "20 to <25"),
      bmi3     = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", "25 to <30"), bmi4   = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", ">=30"),
      met_no   = lvl(e, "met_grp", "Not metastatic"),
      met_yes  = lvl(e, "met_grp", "Metastatic"),
      age_lt70 = lvl(e, "age_grp", "<70"),     age_ge70 = lvl(e, "age_grp", ">=70"),
      sarc_no  = lvl(e, "sarc_grp", "Non-sarcopenic"),
      sarc_yes = lvl(e, "sarc_grp", "Sarcopenic"))
  })
}

# Manuscript-style heatmap: continuous yellow->red, N in every column header,
# eGFR type merged down the first column, black rules between type blocks.
final_ft <- function(tab, title) {
  cols  <- FINAL_SUB_COLS
  spanv <- c("", "", "", "Sex", "BMI category (kg/m²)", "Metastatic disease",
             "Age (years)", "Body composition")
  spanw <- c(1, 1, 1, 2, 4, 2, 2, 2)
  blk   <- officer::fp_border(color = "black", width = 1.5)

  ft <- flextable::flextable(tab, col_keys = c("type", "label", cols))
  ft <- flextable::set_header_labels(ft,
          values = c(list(type = "eGFR type", label = "Equation"),
                     as.list(FINAL_SUB_LABS)))
  ft <- flextable::add_header_row(ft, top = TRUE, values = spanv, colwidths = spanw)
  ft <- flextable::add_header_row(ft, top = TRUE, values = title,
                                  colwidths = 2 + length(cols))
  for (cc in cols) {
    v  <- tab[[cc]]
    ft <- flextable::bg(ft, j = cc, bg = ramp_fill(v, CONT_STOPS, 30), part = "body")
    dark <- which(!is.na(v) & v >= 20)
    if (length(dark))
      ft <- flextable::color(ft, i = dark, j = cc, color = "white", part = "body")
  }
  ft <- flextable::merge_v(ft, j = "type", part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::valign(ft, j = "type", valign = "top", part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = cols, align = "center", part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, i = 2, align = "center", part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, i = 1, align = "left",   part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::bold(ft, part = "header")
  # Black rules closing each eGFR-type block, plus one under the header.
  ft <- flextable::hline(ft, i = FINAL_RULES, border = blk, part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::hline_bottom(ft, border = blk, part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, size = 9, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, i = 1, size = 11, part = "header")
  # Breathing room between the category line and its "N = n" line.
  ft <- flextable::line_spacing(ft, space = 1.5, part = "header")
  flextable::set_table_properties(ft, layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}

# Emit all 10 drugs x over/under for one scale. Call inside results='asis'.
emit_final <- function(cl, scale, scale_label) {
  cat("\n\n## ", scale_label, "\n\n", sep = "")
  for (d in FINAL_DRUGS) {
    cat("\n\n### ", d$lab, "\n\n", sep = "")
    for (dir in c("Overdose", "Underdose")) {
      ft <- final_ft(final_subgroup_table(cl, d$id, dir), paste0(toupper(dir), " (%)"))
      save_ft_docx(ft, paste0("final_", scale, "_", d$id, "_", tolower(dir)))
      cat(flextable::flextable_to_rmd(ft)); cat("\n\n")
    }
    cat(sprintf(
      "[📄 Overdose Word](../tables/heatmap/final_%1$s_%2$s_overdose.docx) · [📄 Underdose Word](../tables/heatmap/final_%1$s_%2$s_underdose.docx)\n\n",
      scale, d$id))
  }
}

# Equations shown in the LOESS panels — all 8. NB: the CKD-EPI Cys 2012 and
# CKD-EPI Cr 2021 panels are partly self-referential (they define the x-axis
# ratio/difference), so interpret those two with care.
LOESS_EQS <- reg$equation

# LOESS: one plot per equation; the 5 drugs are overlaid as colour-coded LOESS
# smooths of P(over/under-dose) vs an x variable (binary 0/1 -> % via mean).
# `xvar`/`xlab`/`xlim` default to the eGFR ratio; the difference set overrides them.
loess_plot <- function(cl, eq, direction, xvar = "egfr_ratio",
                       xlab = "eGFR ratio  (CKD-EPI Cys 2012 / Cr 2021)",
                       xlim = c(0.4, 1.4), pctd_axis = FALSE) {
  r   <- reg[reg$equation == eq, ]
  ttl <- paste0(r$type, " · ", r$label)
  d <- cl %>%
    dplyr::filter(equation == eq, !is.na(cls), !is.na(.data[[xvar]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(y = as.integer(cls == direction) * 100,
                  Drug = factor(drug, levels = DRUG_IDS, labels = DRUG_LABS))
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(.data[[xvar]], y, colour = Drug, fill = Drug))
  # pctd_axis = TRUE gives the Grant-page x axis: -10 % dashed marker under the
  # curves, 10-point ticks with % labels. Used by the % difference set only.
  if (pctd_axis) p <- p + ref_vline()
  p <- p +
    ggplot2::geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, span = 0.9,
                         se = TRUE, alpha = 0.10, linewidth = 0.9) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = xlab, y = paste0("% ", tolower(direction), "d"),
                  title = ttl, colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right",
                   plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
  if (pctd_axis) p <- p + pctd_x()
  p
}
# X-axis for the difference LOESS set (indexed Cys − Cr, mL/min/1.73 m²).
DIFF_XLAB <- "eGFR difference  (CKD-EPI Cys 2012 − Cr 2021, mL/min/1.73 m²)"
DIFF_XLIM <- c(-50, 20)
# X-axis for the % difference LOESS set ((Cys − Cr)/Cr × 100; scale-invariant).
# Axis treatment copied from the Grant page — 10-point ticks with % labels and a
# black dashed marker at -10 % — but the window is sized to THIS index, which sits
# further negative than the Grant page's (median -16 %, range -69..+80):
# [-60, 30] holds 98.3 % of patients and keeps the smooth off the sparse tails.
PCTD_XLAB   <- "eGFR % difference  [(CKD-EPI Cys 2012 − Cr 2021) / Cr 2021, %]"
PCTD_XLIM   <- c(-60, 30)
PCTD_BREAKS <- seq(-80, 80, 10)   # spans the full data range; clipped panels drop the extras
REF_LINE    <- -10
BINW        <- 5                  # histogram bin width, percentage points
CARBO_RED   <- "#F8766D"          # ggplot's hue for the carboplatin ±20% line

# Tick styling shared by every x axis in the carboplatin section: black ticks,
# no minor grid. `pct` appends "%" to the labels — the absolute-difference
# sensitivity panels pass FALSE, where a "%" would be wrong.
tick_x <- function(breaks, pct = TRUE) {
  list(
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks,
                                labels = if (pct) paste0(breaks, "%") else breaks,
                                minor_breaks = NULL),
    ggplot2::theme(
      axis.ticks.x        = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.ticks.length.x = grid::unit(4, "pt"),
      panel.grid.minor.x  = ggplot2::element_blank()))
}
pctd_x <- function() tick_x(PCTD_BREAKS)

# --- Section 14 sensitivity definitions of "eGFR difference" ---------------
# 1) The plain difference Cys − Cr, taken on the INDEXED scale (DIFF_XLAB /
#    DIFF_XLIM above). Unlike the % version it is NOT scale-invariant, so the
#    scale is stated on the axis. Its dashed marker sits at 0 — the two
#    equations agree — since -10 is a percentage and means nothing here.
DIFF_BREAKS <- seq(-80, 40, 10)
# 2) BSA-adjusted eGFRcr-cys against Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance,
#    both in absolute mL/min, as a percentage of Cockcroft-Gault. Window and
#    breaks ported unchanged from the grant page, which plots this index.
PCTD_CG_XLAB   <- "eGFR % difference  [(CKD-EPI Cr-Cys 2021 − Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault, %]"
PCTD_CG_XLIM   <- c(-50, 40)
PCTD_CG_BREAKS <- seq(-60, 60, 10)
ref_vline <- function() {
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = REF_LINE, linetype = "dashed",
                      colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5)
}

# Overdose curve superimposed on the cohort distribution — the Grant page's
# Figure 3, generalised to any equation. Carboplatin ±20 % overdose LOESS (black,
# thick, left axis 0-100 %) over a histogram of the x variable (bars, right axis
# = count). Bars are drawn as a fraction of the tallest bin (rounded up to a clean
# 25) so both series share one panel; the right axis inverts that transform.
# The curve is clipped to [0, 100] exactly as on the Grant page.
overlay_plot <- function(cl, eq, xvar = "egfr_pctdiff", xlab = PCTD_XLAB,
                         xlim = PCTD_XLIM, drug_id = "carboplatin_b20",
                         binw = BINW, pct_axis = TRUE, ref_at = REF_LINE,
                         data = dat, xscale = NULL) {
  r   <- reg[reg$equation == eq, ]
  ttl <- paste0(r$type, " · ", r$label)

  xall  <- data[[xvar]]; xall <- xall[!is.na(xall)]
  n_tot <- length(xall)
  brks  <- seq(floor(min(xall) / binw) * binw, ceiling(max(xall) / binw) * binw, binw)
  cnt_max <- .nice_max(max(graphics::hist(xall, breaks = brks, plot = FALSE)$counts))

  d <- cl %>%
    dplyr::filter(equation == eq, drug == drug_id, !is.na(cls), !is.na(.data[[xvar]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(y = as.integer(cls == "Overdose") * 100)
  fit  <- stats::loess(y ~ x, span = 0.9, data = data.frame(x = d[[xvar]], y = d$y))
  gx   <- seq(xlim[1], xlim[2], length.out = 200)
  pr   <- stats::predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x = gx), se = TRUE)
  clip <- function(v) pmin(pmax(v, 0), 100)
  ov   <- data.frame(x = gx, fit = clip(pr$fit),
                     lo = clip(pr$fit - 1.96 * pr$se.fit),
                     hi = clip(pr$fit + 1.96 * pr$se.fit))

  p <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_histogram(
      data = data.frame(x = xall),
      ggplot2::aes(x, y = ggplot2::after_stat(count) / cnt_max * 100),
      binwidth = binw, boundary = 0,
      fill = CARBO_RED, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = 0.55)
  if (!is.null(ref_at))
    p <- p + ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = ref_at, linetype = "dashed",
                                 colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5)
  p <- p +
    ggplot2::geom_ribbon(data = ov, ggplot2::aes(x, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
                         fill = "black", alpha = 0.12) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(data = ov, ggplot2::aes(x, y = fit),
                       colour = "black", linewidth = 1.7)
  # `xscale` wins when given (the sensitivity panels); otherwise the default
  # percentage ticks, so every existing call behaves exactly as before.
  if (!is.null(xscale)) p <- p + xscale else if (pct_axis) p <- p + pctd_x()
  p +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      name = "% overdosed  (carboplatin ±20%)", breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
      sec.axis = ggplot2::sec_axis(~ . / 100 * cnt_max, name = "Number of participants",
                                   breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(5))) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim, ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = xlab, title = ttl,
      subtitle = sprintf("Black line = %% overdosed (left axis) · bars = distribution (right axis) · N = %s",
                         format(n_tot, big.mark = ","))) +
    .overlay_theme()
}

# Shared look for every panel in the "Carboplatin 20 % plots" section: pink
# distribution on the right axis, black overdose series on the left.
.overlay_theme <- function() {
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title         = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      plot.subtitle      = ggplot2::element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey30"),
      axis.title.y.right = ggplot2::element_text(colour = CARBO_RED),
      axis.text.y.right  = ggplot2::element_text(colour = CARBO_RED),
      panel.grid.minor   = ggplot2::element_blank())
}
# Round a count up to a clean axis maximum, with ~15 % headroom so the tallest
# bar stops short of the panel top and the black overdose line stays readable
# over it. Step scales with magnitude.
.nice_max <- function(mx) {
  mx   <- mx * 1.15
  step <- if (mx <= 20) 5 else if (mx <= 50) 10 else 25
  ceiling(mx / step) * step
}

# Discrete-marker twin of overlay_plot: bars = the share of the cohort in each
# category (pink, right axis); black line+points = the share of that category
# overdosed (left axis). Same colours, axes and theme as the continuous panels,
# so the four markers read as one set.
bar_line_plot <- function(cl, eq, grpcol, xlab, drug_id = "carboplatin_b20") {
  r   <- reg[reg$equation == eq, ]
  ttl <- paste0(r$type, " · ", r$label)
  agg <- cl %>%
    dplyr::filter(equation == eq, drug == drug_id, !is.na(cls), !is.na(.data[[grpcol]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(grp = droplevels(.data[[grpcol]])) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(grp) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(N = dplyr::n(),
                     pct_over = mean(cls == "Overdose") * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(grp) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pct_cohort = N / sum(N) * 100)
  n_tot   <- sum(agg$N)
  cnt_max <- ceiling(max(agg$pct_cohort) * 1.15 / 10) * 10   # headroom, as above
  xl <- paste0(levels(agg$grp), "\n(N=", agg$N, ")")

  ggplot2::ggplot(agg, ggplot2::aes(x = as.integer(grp))) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(ggplot2::aes(y = pct_cohort / cnt_max * 100),
                      fill = CARBO_RED, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3,
                      alpha = 0.55, width = 0.68) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = pct_over), colour = "black", linewidth = 1.7) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(y = pct_over), colour = "black", size = 2.8) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(xl), labels = xl) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
      name = "% overdosed  (carboplatin ±20%)", breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
      sec.axis = ggplot2::sec_axis(~ . / 100 * cnt_max, name = "% of cohort",
                                   breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(5))) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      x = xlab, title = ttl,
      subtitle = sprintf("Black line = %% overdosed (left axis) · bars = %% of cohort (right axis) · N = %s",
                         format(n_tot, big.mark = ","))) +
    .overlay_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank())
}
# X-axis for the measured-GFR LOESS set (the reference itself; indexed vs absolute).
MGFR_XLAB_IDX <- "Measured GFR  (⁵¹Cr-EDTA, mL/min/1.73 m²)"
MGFR_XLIM_IDX <- c(15, 145)
MGFR_XLAB_NIX <- "Measured GFR  (⁵¹Cr-EDTA, absolute mL/min)"
MGFR_XLIM_NIX <- c(15, 185)
# X-axis for the muscle Z-score LOESS (465 body-comp cohort).
MZ_XLAB <- "Muscle Z-score (SMI)"
MZ_XLIM <- c(-3, 2)

# ECOG distribution: % over/under-dose by ECOG group (0 / 1 / ≥2), one line per
# drug, per equation. N per ECOG group is annotated on the x-axis labels.
# Grouped-bar plot of % over/under-dose by a categorical group (`grpcol`); 5 drug
# bars per group, sorted low->high. Used for ECOG and Fried frailty.
ecog_plot <- function(cl, eq, direction, grpcol = "ecog_grp", xlab = "ECOG performance status", ymax = NA) {
  r <- reg[reg$equation == eq, ]; ttl <- paste0(r$type, " · ", r$label)
  s <- cl %>%
    dplyr::filter(equation == eq, !is.na(cls), !is.na(.data[[grpcol]])) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Drug = factor(drug, levels = DRUG_IDS, labels = DRUG_LABS),
                  grp  = .data[[grpcol]])
  agg <- s %>% dplyr::group_by(grp, Drug) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(pct = mean(cls == direction) * 100, .groups = "drop_last") %>%
    dplyr::arrange(pct, .by_group = TRUE) %>%        # low -> high within each group
    dplyr::mutate(xpos = as.integer(grp) + (dplyr::row_number() - 3) * 0.17) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
  ns <- s %>% dplyr::filter(drug == DRUG_IDS[1]) %>% dplyr::count(grp)
  xl <- paste0(levels(s$grp), "\n(N=",
               ns$n[match(levels(s$grp), as.character(ns$grp))], ")")
  ggplot2::ggplot(agg, ggplot2::aes(xpos, pct, fill = Drug)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.16) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(xl), labels = xl) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, ymax)) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = xlab, y = paste0("% ", tolower(direction), "d"),
                  title = ttl, fill = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "right",
                   plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
}

# Emit every drug × direction for one scale/version (call inside a results='asis'
# chunk). Saves each table to Word and prints it with a download link.
emit_scale <- function(cl, version, scale, scale_label, extra = FALSE, prefix = version) {
  cat("\n\n### ", scale_label, "\n\n", sep = "")
  for (d in DRUGS) {
    cat("\n\n#### ", d$lab, "\n\n", sep = "")
    for (dir in c("Overdose", "Underdose")) {
      fname <- paste0(prefix, "_", scale, "_", d$id, "_", tolower(dir))
      ft <- build_ft(cl, d$id, dir, version, extra)
      save_ft_docx(ft, fname)
      cat(flextable::flextable_to_rmd(ft))
      cat("\n\n")
    }
    cat(sprintf(
      "[📄 Overdose Word](../tables/heatmap/%1$s_%2$s_%3$s_overdose.docx) · [📄 Underdose Word](../tables/heatmap/%1$s_%2$s_%3$s_underdose.docx)\n\n",
      prefix, scale, d$id))
  }
}

# --- Most conservative GFR = per-patient MINIMUM of CKD-EPI Cr 2021,
# Cockcroft-Gault, and CKD-EPI Cr-Cys 2021 (the lowest / dose-limiting estimate).
build_mcg_long <- function(scale) {
  col_of <- function(eq) {
    r <- reg[reg$equation == eq, ]
    if (scale == "index") r$index_col[[1]] else r$nonindex_col[[1]]
  }
  mgfr <- dat[[MGFR[[scale]]]]
  mcg  <- pmin(dat[[col_of("CKDEPIcr21")]], dat[[col_of("CG")]],
               dat[[col_of("CKDEPIcrcys21")]], na.rm = TRUE)
  base <- dplyr::select(dat, sex, bmi_grp, met_grp, age_grp)
  tier <- purrr::map_dfr(TIER_DRUGS, function(dr)
    dplyr::bind_cols(base, tibble::tibble(drug = dr, cls = dose_class_tier(mcg, mgfr, dr))))
  carbo <- purrr::map_dfr(names(CARBO_BANDS), function(bn) {
    k <- CARBO_BANDS[[bn]]
    dplyr::bind_cols(base, tibble::tibble(drug = bn,
                                          cls = carbo_class(mcg, mgfr, k[["k_hi"]], k[["k_lo"]])))
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(tier, carbo)
}
mcg_index    <- build_mcg_long("index")
mcg_nonindex <- build_mcg_long("nonindex")

# One table: rows = drugs, columns = subgroups, for the most-conservative GFR.
mcg_table <- function(cl, direction) {
  pct <- function(x) if (nrow(x)) round(mean(x$cls == direction) * 100, 1) else NA_real_
  lvl <- function(x, col, v) pct(x[!is.na(x[[col]]) & x[[col]] == v, ])
  per_drug <- function(dr) {
    e <- cl[cl$drug == dr, ]
    tibble::tibble(drug = dr, Overall = pct(e),
      Female = lvl(e, "sex", "Female"), Male = lvl(e, "sex", "Male"),
      bmi1 = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", "<20"), bmi2 = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", "20 to <25"),
      bmi3 = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", "25 to <30"), bmi4 = lvl(e, "bmi_grp", ">=30"),
      met_no = lvl(e, "met_grp", "Not metastatic"), met_yes = lvl(e, "met_grp", "Metastatic"),
      age_lt70 = lvl(e, "age_grp", "<70"), age_ge70 = lvl(e, "age_grp", ">=70"))
  }
  purrr::map_dfr(DRUG_IDS, per_drug) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Drug = factor(drug, levels = DRUG_IDS, labels = DRUG_LABS)) %>%
    dplyr::select(Drug, dplyr::all_of(SUB_COLS))
}

# Flextable for the drug-row table (Drug label column + subgroup spanners).
make_mcg_ft <- function(tab, title, fill_fn, dark_fn) {
  ncol_total <- length(c("Drug", SUB_COLS))
  ft <- flextable::flextable(tab, col_keys = c("Drug", SUB_COLS))
  ft <- flextable::set_header_labels(ft, values = c(list(Drug = "Drug"), as.list(SUB_LABS)))
  ft <- flextable::add_header_row(ft, top = TRUE,
    values    = c("", "", "Sex", "BMI category (kg/m²)", "Metastatic disease", "Age (years)"),
    colwidths = c(1, 1, 2, 4, 2, 2))
  ft <- flextable::add_header_row(ft, top = TRUE, values = title, colwidths = ncol_total)
  for (cc in SUB_COLS) {
    v  <- tab[[cc]]
    ft <- flextable::bg(ft, j = cc, bg = fill_fn(v), part = "body")
    dark <- which(dark_fn(v))
    if (length(dark)) ft <- flextable::color(ft, i = dark, j = cc, color = "white", part = "body")
  }
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = SUB_COLS, align = "center", part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, i = 2, align = "center", part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, i = 1, align = "left",   part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::bold(ft, part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, size = 9, part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, i = 1, size = 11, part = "header")
  flextable::set_table_properties(ft, layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}

mcg_ft <- function(cl, direction, version) {
  title <- paste0(toupper(direction), " (%)")
  if (version == "cat") {
    fill_fn <- cat4_fill;                                 dark_fn <- function(x) !is.na(x) & x >= 10
  } else {
    fill_fn <- function(x) ramp_fill(x, CONT_STOPS, 30);  dark_fn <- function(x) !is.na(x) & x >= 20
  }
  make_mcg_ft(mcg_table(cl, direction), title, fill_fn, dark_fn)
}

emit_mcg <- function(cl, version, scale, scale_label) {
  cat("\n\n#### ", scale_label, "\n\n", sep = "")
  for (dir in c("Overdose", "Underdose")) {
    ft <- mcg_ft(cl, dir, version)
    save_ft_docx(ft, paste0("mcg_", version, "_", scale, "_", tolower(dir)))
    cat(flextable::flextable_to_rmd(ft)); cat("\n\n")
  }
  cat(sprintf(
    "[📄 Overdose Word](../tables/heatmap/mcg_%1$s_%2$s_overdose.docx) · [📄 Underdose Word](../tables/heatmap/mcg_%1$s_%2$s_underdose.docx)\n\n",
    version, scale))
}

# ===== TABLE 1 — Fried frailty cohort ======================================
# Baseline characteristics of the 592 patients who have a Fried class,
# stratified by that class. Row set and row order follow the manuscript
# template exactly. Tests: Kruskal-Wallis across the three classes for
# continuous rows (no normality assumed; several of these are skewed), and
# chi-square for categorical rows, or Fisher's exact (Monte Carlo) when any
# expected count is below 5. A multi-level variable carries one p-value, on
# its header row. Every variable in this table is complete in the source
# file, so there is no "n observed" column.
T1_LEVELS <- c("Non-frail", "Pre-frail", "Frail")
T1_IND    <- strrep("\u00A0", 4)   # indent for the levels of a categorical row

t1_mean_sd <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  if (!length(x)) return("—")
  sprintf("%.*f (%.*f)", digits, mean(x), digits, stats::sd(x))
}
t1_med_iqr <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  if (!length(x)) return("—")
  q <- stats::quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
  sprintf("%.*f [%.*f–%.*f]", digits, q[[2]], digits, q[[1]], digits, q[[3]])
}
t1_msd2 <- function(x) t1_mean_sd(x, 2)
t1_mi2  <- function(x) t1_med_iqr(x, 2)
t1_n_pct <- function(f) {
  n <- sum(!is.na(f)); if (!n) return("—")
  k <- sum(f, na.rm = TRUE); sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", k, k / n * 100)
}
t1_p_tab <- function(tab) {
  if (any(dim(tab) < 2) || sum(tab) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  ex <- suppressWarnings(stats::chisq.test(tab)$expected)
  if (any(ex < 5)) stats::fisher.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 20000)$p.value
  else suppressWarnings(stats::chisq.test(tab)$p.value)
}
# `lvl = TRUE` marks an indented level of a categorical variable; those print
# unbolded, everything else bold.
t1_row <- function(label, vals, p = NA_real_, lvl = FALSE) {
  tibble::tibble(label = label, Overall = vals[[1]],
                 `Non-frail` = vals[[2]], `Pre-frail` = vals[[3]], Frail = vals[[4]],
                 p = p, lvl = lvl)
}
# One continuous row; `fmt` is t1_mean_sd, t1_med_iqr or a fixed-digit variant.
t1_cont <- function(d, var, label, fmt = t1_med_iqr) {
  x  <- d[[var]]; g <- d$fried_grp
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(g)
  x  <- x[ok]; g <- factor(g[ok], levels = T1_LEVELS)
  p  <- if (nlevels(droplevels(g)) > 1) stats::kruskal.test(x, g)$p.value else NA_real_
  t1_row(label, c(list(fmt(x)), lapply(T1_LEVELS, function(l) fmt(x[g == l]))), p)
}
# One binary row from a logical vector aligned to `d`.
t1_bin <- function(d, flag, label) {
  g  <- d$fried_grp; ok <- !is.na(flag) & !is.na(g)
  f  <- flag[ok]; g <- factor(g[ok], levels = T1_LEVELS)
  t1_row(label, c(list(t1_n_pct(f)), lapply(T1_LEVELS, function(l) t1_n_pct(f[g == l]))),
         t1_p_tab(table(f, g)))
}
# A categorical variable: a header row carrying the one p-value for the whole
# variable, then one indented row per level.
t1_cat <- function(d, var, label) {
  v  <- d[[var]]; g <- d$fried_grp; ok <- !is.na(v) & !is.na(g)
  v  <- droplevels(factor(v[ok])); g <- factor(g[ok], levels = T1_LEVELS)
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    t1_row(label, as.list(rep("", 4)), t1_p_tab(table(v, g))),
    purrr::map_dfr(levels(v), function(l) {
      f <- v == l
      t1_row(paste0(T1_IND, l),
             c(list(t1_n_pct(f)), lapply(T1_LEVELS, function(k) t1_n_pct(f[g == k]))),
             lvl = TRUE)
    }))
}

build_table1 <- function(data = dat) {
  d  <- data %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(fried_grp))
  g  <- factor(d$fried_grp, levels = T1_LEVELS)
  nn <- c(nrow(d), as.integer(table(g)[T1_LEVELS]))
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    t1_row("N", as.list(format(nn, big.mark = ","))),
    t1_bin(d, d$sex == "Male", "Males (n, %)"),
    t1_cont(d, "age", "Age (mean (SD))", t1_mean_sd),
    t1_bin(d, d$age65, "≥65 years (n, %)"),
    t1_cont(d, "weight", "Weight in kg (median [IQR])"),
    t1_cont(d, "height", "Height in cm (median [IQR])"),
    t1_cont(d, "BSA", "BSA m² (median [IQR])", t1_mi2),
    t1_cont(d, "BMI", "BMI kg/m² (median [IQR])"),
    t1_cat(d, "bmi_who", "BMI category (n, %)"),
    t1_cat(d, "smoke_grp", "Smoking status (n, %)"),
    t1_bin(d, d$hypertension == 1, "Hypertension (n, %)"),
    t1_bin(d, d$diabetes == 1, "Diabetes (n, %)"),
    t1_cont(d, "Hb", "Hemoglobin g/dL (median [IQR])"),
    t1_cont(d, "Alb", "Serum albumin g/dL (median [IQR])"),
    t1_cont(d, "CRP", "CRP mg/L (median [IQR])"),
    t1_cont(d, "mGFRindex", "mGFRadj mL/min per 1.73 m² (mean (SD))", t1_mean_sd),
    t1_cont(d, "Cr", "Creatinine mg/dL (median [IQR])", t1_mi2),
    t1_cont(d, "CysC", "Cystatin C mg/L (median [IQR])", t1_mi2),
    t1_cat(d, "site_grp", "Cancer site (n, %)"),
    t1_cat(d, "stage_grp", "Cancer stage (%)"),
    t1_bin(d, d$met_grp == "Metastatic", "Metastatic disease"),
    t1_cat(d, "ecog_grp", "ECOG performance status (%)"))
}

# Render Table 1: bold every variable label, leave the indented levels plain,
# rule between rows, p-values to three decimals.
table1_ft <- function(tb) {
  thin <- officer::fp_border(color = "#BFBFBF", width = 0.5)
  blk  <- officer::fp_border(color = "black", width = 1.5)
  body <- tb %>%
    dplyr::mutate(p = dplyr::case_when(is.na(p) ~ "", p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
                                       TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p))) %>%
    dplyr::select(-lvl)
  ft <- flextable::flextable(body)
  ft <- flextable::set_header_labels(ft, values = list(
    label = "Characteristic", Overall = "Overall",
    `Non-frail` = "Non-frail", `Pre-frail` = "Pre-frail", Frail = "Frail", p = "p"))
  ft <- flextable::bold(ft, i = which(!tb$lvl), j = "label", part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = c("Overall", T1_LEVELS, "p"),
                         align = "center", part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::align(ft, j = "label", align = "left", part = "all")
  ft <- flextable::bold(ft, part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::hline(ft, border = thin, part = "body")
  ft <- flextable::hline_bottom(ft, border = blk, part = "header")
  ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft, size = 9, part = "all")
  flextable::set_table_properties(ft, layout = "autofit", width = 1)
}

3 Overview

For every patient we compute the chemotherapy dose each estimated-GFR (eGFR) equation would prescribe and compare it to the dose that measured GFR (mGFR, ⁵¹Cr-EDTA clearance) — the gold standard — would prescribe. Each cell is the percent of patients mis-dosed in that subgroup:

  • OVERDOSE (%) — the equation would give more drug than mGFR warrants.
  • UNDERDOSE (%) — the equation would give less drug than mGFR warrants.

Cell colour — the number in each cell is the share of patients in that subgroup whose dose would be wrong in that direction (over- or under-dosed vs mGFR). The same tables are shown in two colour versions so you can compare:

  • Part A — categorical (4 severity bands):  yellow < 5 %  ·  orange 5–10 %  ·  red 10–20 %  ·  purple > 20 % .
  • Part B — continuous: a shade of the value,  yellow = 0 %  →  orange  →  deep red , saturating (worst) at ≥ 30 %.

Both are severity scales (higher % = worse) applied to over- and under-dose alike; the exact percentage is printed in every cell.

Columns give the Overall rate and rates within Sex, BMI category, Metastatic disease, and Age (<70 vs ≥70) subgroups. Results are shown on both the indexed (mL/min/1.73 m²) and non-indexed (absolute mL/min) GFR scale; mGFR is always taken on the same scale as the equation. All 1,200 patients are used for every drug (a counterfactual — the file has no administered doses).

Dosing rules — one row per GFR band. Tier is the ordered dose code used internally (higher = more drug; 0 = avoid / forced reduce).

Drug GFR (mL/min) Dose Tier
Cisplatin ≥ 60 Full dose 3
50 – 59 −25 % 2
40 – 49 −50 % 1
< 40 Avoid 0
Methotrexate (ADDIKD) ≥ 60 Full dose 3
45 – 59.99 −25 % 2
30 – 44.99 −50 % 1
< 30 Avoid 0
Melphalan (200 mg/m²) > 60 Full, 200 mg/m² 2
30 – 59 140 mg/m² 1
< 30 Forced reduce, 140 mg/m² 0
Carboplatin (Calvert) continuous (AUC) dose = target AUC × (GFR + 25), target AUC 5; over-/under-dose set by a ±20 % or ±15 % band — see note below —
NoteHow carboplatin over- and under-dosing are defined

Carboplatin is not dosed in GFR tiers like the other three drugs — it is dosed to a target drug exposure with the Calvert formula: dose (mg) = target AUC × (GFR + 25), with target AUC = 5. Because the dose is directly proportional to the GFR entered, plugging an eGFR equation into the formula instead of the true (measured) GFR changes the dose by the same percentage that the equation mis-estimates GFR. We flag only a clinically meaningful error, using a tolerance band around the AUC-5 target:

  • Overdose — the eGFR-based dose is larger than the dose from measured GFR at AUC 6. Since AUC 6 is 20 % above AUC 5, the equation would deliver > 20 % too much carboplatin.
  • Underdose — the eGFR-based dose is smaller than the dose from measured GFR at AUC 4 (20 % below AUC 5) → > 20 % too little.

That ±20 % band is reported as carboplatin_b20; carboplatin_b15 repeats the same test with a tighter ±15 % band (AUC 5.75 and 4.25). Both are shown because the analysis plan asked for 15 % and 20 % thresholds. (These definitions come from the eligibility-cutoffs document.)

Note

“Metastatic disease — Unknown” from the source template is omitted because metastatic status is complete (no missing) in this dataset. The creatinine equation shown is CKD-EPI 2021 (the race-free version present in the data).

4 Variable codebook

Every field used to build the tables. Inputs are columns read from OncoGFR1200_MGH_chemo_CJASN.xlsx (N = 1,200); derived fields are computed in this analysis.

Kidney-function inputs (eGFR / mGFR)

Each equation is stored twice — an index column (mL/min/1.73 m², BSA-normalised) and a non-index column (absolute mL/min ≈ indexed × BSA ⁄ 1.73). Measured GFR is the reference all equations are compared against; comparisons are made on the matching scale.

eGFR type Equation (label) Index column Non-index column
reference Measured GFR (⁵¹Cr-EDTA) mGFRindex mGFRnon_index
eGFRcr CKD-EPI 2021 (creatinine) CKDEPIcr21index CKDEPIcr21non_index
eGFRcr EKFC 2021 (creatinine) EKFCcrindex EKFCcrnon_index
eGFRcys CKD-EPI 2012 (cystatin C) CKDEPIcysindex CKDEPIcysnon_index
eGFRcys EKFC 2023 (cystatin C) EKFCcysindex EKFCcysnon_index
eGFRcr-cys CKD-EPI 2021 (Cr–Cys) CKDEPIcrcys21index CKDEPIcrcys21non_index
eGFRcr-cys EKFC 2023 (Cr–Cys) EKFCcrcysindex EKFCcrcysnon-index
ClCr Cockcroft–Gault CGindex CGnon_index
Panel CKD-EPI 4-marker (Cr, Cys, β2M, BTP) CKDEPI4mark CKDEPI4marknon_index

Underlying labs (Cr, CysC, B2M, BTP) and anthropometrics (weight, height, BSA, age, gender) were used upstream to compute these equation values; this analysis reads only the equation columns plus gender, BMI, and metastasis (below).

Subgroup variables (table columns)

Derived field Source column Levels / definition
Overall — all 1,200 patients
sex gender (1, 2) Male (1); Female (2)
bmi_grp BMI (kg/m²) <20; 20 to <25; 25 to <30; ≥30
met_grp metastasis (0, 1) Not metastatic (0); Metastatic (1)
age_grp age (years) <70; ≥70 (binary cut-off at 70)
sarc_grp sarcopenia_prado (OncoGFR_MGH_final_0428.xlsx, joined on protocol) Non-sarcopenic (0); Sarcopenic (1). Only the 465 body-comp patients (in_bodycomp) — used in the 465 section.

eGFR difference definitions (the figure x-axes)

Three ways of expressing how far a cystatin-informed estimate sits from a creatinine one. Section 14 shows all three against the same outcome; Sections 9–11 use the first two.

Variable Definition Scale Used by
egfr_ratio CKDEPIcysindex / CKDEPIcr21index scale-invariant (the BSA factor cancels) Section 9
egfr_diff CKDEPIcysindex − CKDEPIcr21index indexed, mL/min/1.73 m² — a difference is not scale-invariant, so the scale matters Section 10; Section 14 Sensitivity 1
egfr_pctdiff (CKDEPIcysindex − CKDEPIcr21index) / CKDEPIcr21index × 100 scale-invariant Section 11; Section 14 primary
egfr_pctdiff_cg (CKDEPIcrcys21non_index − CGnon_index) / CGnon_index × 100 absolute mL/min (actual BSA), as specified Section 14 Sensitivity 2; the grant figures

egfr_pctdiff and egfr_pctdiff_cg are both percentages but they are not the same quantity: the first compares CKD-EPI Cys 2012 with CKD-EPI Cr 2021, the second compares CKD-EPI Cr-Cys 2021 with Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance.

Table 1 fields (Section 16)

Derived only for Table 1, which follows the manuscript template rather than this page’s subgroup definitions.

Field Source Definition
age65 age age >= 65.
bmi_who BMI WHO bands: Underweight <18.5 · Normal 18.5–24.9 · Overweight 25–29.9 · Obese ≥30. Not bmi_grp, whose <20 / 20–25 / 25–30 / ≥30 cuts drive the heatmap subgroup columns and are matched by string in several lookups.
smoke_grp Smoking Never (0) · Former (2) · Current (1). The coding is not the intuitive order — verified against the file’s never.smoker / former.smoker / current.smoker indicator columns, which agree exactly with 0 = never (604), 1 = current (128), 2 = former (468).
stage_grp stage 1 · 2 · 3 · 4 · Not applicable (code 5). All 55 patients in code 5 carry stageV, and 43 of them TIS.
site_grp site.ajcc The 11 cancer-site groups of the template, via SITE_LABS. Codes 6, 7, 9 and 11 are fixed by their sex distribution (Breast, Female reproductive organs, Endocrine system, Male genital organs); the other seven print as their code pending a codebook.

Computed classification fields

Field Values Meaning
drug cisplatin, methotrexate, melphalan, carboplatin_b20, carboplatin_b15 which drug’s dosing rule was applied. carboplatin_b20 and carboplatin_b15 are the same carboplatin analysis run with a ±20 % vs ±15 % tolerance band (see the carboplatin note under Overview).
dose_tier 0–3 ordered dose level from the rule (see Dosing rules); higher = more drug, 0 = avoid
dose_class (cls) Overdose / Underdose / Concordant equation’s tier vs mGFR’s tier (Calvert band for carboplatin)
pct_over 0–100 % of the subgroup classified Overdose → OVERDOSE (%) cells
pct_under 0–100 % of the subgroup classified Underdose → UNDERDOSE (%) cells
equation / type / label — equation id / eGFR family / display name (see table above)

Cell colour: two versions of the same tables — Part A categorical (yellow <5 / orange 5–10 / red 10–20 / purple >20) and Part B continuous yellow→red (worst at ≥30 %). Higher % = worse in both; the number is printed in every cell.

5 Part A — Categorical colour (4 levels)

Severity bands (same scale for over- and under-dose):  yellow < 5 %  ·  orange 5–10 %  ·  red 10–20 %  ·  purple > 20 %

📄 Overdose Word · 📄 Underdose Word

7 Most conservative GFR — over/under-dose heatmap

Most conservative GFR = for each patient, the lowest of three estimates — CKD-EPI Cr (2021), Cockcroft-Gault, and CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (2021) — i.e. the dose-limiting (safest) value. Rows = drugs, columns = subgroups; each cell is the % over- or under-dosed vs measured GFR when this single conservative estimate drives the dose. Because it takes the lowest GFR it gives the lowest overdose rate of the three inputs (over-dosing only when all three still exceed mGFR), at the cost of more underdosing. Both colour versions and both GFR scales are shown; the exact % is printed in every cell.

Part A — Categorical colour (4 levels)

9 LOESS — over/under-dose probability vs eGFR ratio (Cys / Cr)

For each of the 8 eGFR equations, a LOESS smooth of the probability that the equation over- (or under-) doses relative to measured GFR (mGFR), as a function of the patient’s eGFR ratio = CKD-EPI Cys (2012) ⁄ CKD-EPI Cr (2021) (ratio of two eGFRs, so BSA cancels and the value is the same on either scale). One plot per equation, with the 5 drugs overlaid as colour-coded curves (shaded band = ± 95 % CI), arranged in four subsections — Indexed → Overdose / Underdose and Non-indexed → Overdose / Underdose (32 plots total). Interpret the CKD-EPI Cys 2012 and CKD-EPI Cr 2021 panels with care — the x-axis ratio is built from those two equations, so those panels are partly self-referential. Same OncoGFR cohort (N = 1,200). The two equation families mirror each other: a low ratio (cystatin-eGFR below creatinine-eGFR — e.g. low muscle mass, where creatinine reads function falsely high) makes creatinine-based equations overdose, whereas a high ratio (cystatin-eGFR above creatinine-eGFR) makes cystatin-based equations overdose. So creatinine-equation overdose curves fall as the ratio rises while cystatin-equation curves rise — exactly what makes this eGFR ratio a useful discriminating biomarker (underdose curves are the mirror image).

Indexed GFR (mL/min/1.73 m²)

Overdose

Code 
emit_plots(lapply(LOESS_EQS, function(eq) loess_plot(cl_index, eq, "Overdose")), "loess-idx-over")

11 LOESS (% difference) — over/under-dose probability vs eGFR % difference

Third LOESS set: the x-axis is the % difference = (eGFR_Cys − eGFR_Cr) ⁄ eGFR_Cr × 100 (CKD-EPI Cys 2012 vs Cr 2021). It is a ratio of two eGFRs, so it is scale-invariant. Positive = cystatin-eGFR above creatinine-eGFR (cystatin reads function higher). Because a higher % difference means cystatin reads GFR higher, creatinine-equation overdose curves fall as the % difference increases while cystatin-equation curves rise — matching the ratio version. The CKD-EPI Cys 2012 and Cr 2021 panels are partly self-referential (they define the x-axis).

The axis treatment is the Grant page’s — 10-point ticks and a black dashed marker at −10 % — with the window sized to this index ([−60, 30], 98.3 % of patients).

Per scale: the 8-equation × 5-drug LOESS panels for over- and under-dose. The carboplatin ±20 % overlay that used to sit here now lives in §14 Carboplatin 20 % plots, alongside the other three frailty markers.

12 LOESS (measured GFR) — over/under-dose probability vs measured GFR

Fourth LOESS set: the x-axis is the reference itself — measured GFR (⁵¹Cr-EDTA) — rather than a Cr‑vs‑Cys discordance. It asks a different question: at what true GFR levels does each equation misdose? All 8 equations, 5 drugs overlaid, index/non-index × over/under (32 plots total). Because over/under-dose is defined by crossing a dosing threshold vs mGFR, the curves peak near each drug’s GFR cutoffs (cisplatin 60/50/40; methotrexate 60/45/30; melphalan 60/30; carboplatin is continuous via Calvert) and fall toward 0 far from them. Every panel here is “self-referential” (mGFR defines the outcome), so read them as where along the true-GFR range the misdosing sits, not as a biomarker-discrimination curve. Indexed vs non-indexed use mGFRindex / mGFRnon_index.

13 Frailty markers — muscle Z-score & ECOG

Two additional views of dosing error against markers of frailty, in the same per-equation / 5-drugs-overlaid format. Over/under-dose is always vs measured GFR. Indexed GFR classification.

Muscle Z-score (LOESS, 465 body-composition cohort)

Y = % over- (or under-) dosed; x = muscle Z-score (SMI). Mechanistically, lower muscle Z (less muscle) lowers serum creatinine, so creatinine-based equations can read GFR falsely high → overdose; cystatin-based equations are muscle-independent. The curves show how this plays out across the muscle spectrum (CIs widen at the sparse extremes). N = 465; indexed GFR.

Z-score provenance. The Z is computed in this document with the bodycompref package (v2.0.1) — reference_z_scores(metric = "SMI", level = "L3", …), a GAMLSS LMSP model fit to Framingham Heart Study CT data (Tonnesen et al., Invest Radiol 2023) — rather than the stored z_score column, which came from an older build with an age floor of 35. ⚠️ Reference window is age 38–80, but this cohort spans 19–86, so 58 / 465 (12.5 %) patients (46 younger than 38, 12 older than 80) are clamped to a boundary age and their Z is anchored to an age they are not — read the extremes of the muscle spectrum with that in mind.

Overdose

Code 
emit_plots(lapply(LOESS_EQS, function(eq) loess_plot(cl_index_465, eq, "Overdose", "muscle_z", MZ_XLAB, MZ_XLIM)), "mz-over")

Derived dose variables

Per-patient binary flags (1 = yes, 0 = no), computed for each equation on the indexed scale vs measured GFR (whole 1,200 cohort):

Variable Definition (per equation, vs mGFR)
cisplatin_eligible equation GFR ≥ 40 → cisplatin-eligible (not “avoid”)
carbo15_over Calvert dose > 15 % above the mGFR AUC-5 dose
carbo15_under Calvert dose > 15 % below the mGFR AUC-5 dose
carbo20_over Calvert dose > 20 % above the mGFR AUC-5 dose
carbo20_under Calvert dose > 20 % below the mGFR AUC-5 dose

The code that creates them (click ▸ Code to expand):

Code 
dose_vars <- purrr::map_dfr(reg$equation, function(eq) {
  g <- dat[[reg$index_col[reg$equation == eq]]]   # this equation's indexed GFR
  m <- dat$mGFRindex                              # measured GFR (indexed)
  tibble::tibble(
    equation = eq, ecog_grp = dat$ecog_grp,
    cisplatin_eligible = as.integer(dose_tier(g, "cisplatin") > 0),
    carbo15_over  = as.integer(carbo_class(g, m, 5.75, 4.25) == "Overdose"),
    carbo15_under = as.integer(carbo_class(g, m, 5.75, 4.25) == "Underdose"),
    carbo20_over  = as.integer(carbo_class(g, m, 6, 4)       == "Overdose"),
    carbo20_under = as.integer(carbo_class(g, m, 6, 4)       == "Underdose"))
}) %>% dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(reg, equation, type, label), by = "equation")

Overall rate (% yes) of each flag, by equation:

Code 
dose_vars %>%
  dplyr::transmute(Equation = paste(type, "·", label),
                   cisplatin_eligible, carbo15_over, carbo15_under, carbo20_over, carbo20_under) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Equation) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), ~ round(mean(.x) * 100, 1)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Equation", "Cispl. eligible %", "Carbo15 over %",
                             "Carbo15 under %", "Carbo20 over %", "Carbo20 under %"))

14 Carboplatin 20 % plots

The four frailty markers against carboplatin ±20 % overdose, on the absolute mL/min (actual BSA) scale, measured GFR as reference — one consistent format throughout:

  • Black line, left axis — the proportion overdosed.
  • Light pink, right axis — how the cohort is distributed: a histogram for continuous markers, bars for discrete ones.
  • One panel per dosing equation (8), so each marker can be read across equations.

Continuous markers (eGFR % difference, muscle Z-score) use LOESS to characterise the unadjusted association, with the smooth clipped to [0, 100]; the shaded band is its 95 % CI. Discrete markers (ECOG, Fried) show the observed proportion per category, joined by the black line.

The eGFR difference is then repeated under two alternative definitions (sensitivity analyses). Only the x axis changes: same cohort, same outcome, same construction, so the three sets are read side by side.

eGFR % difference (whole 1,200 cohort)

Primary definition — (CKD-EPI Cys 2012 − CKD-EPI Cr 2021) / CKD-EPI Cr 2021, as a percentage. Scale-invariant: the BSA factor cancels, so indexed and actual-BSA values are identical.

Code 
emit_plots(lapply(LOESS_EQS, function(eq) overlay_plot(cl_nonindex, eq)), "carbo20-egfrdiff")

<U+2B07><U+FE0F> Download these panels as PowerPoint (editable)

Sensitivity 1 — absolute eGFR difference (Cys − Cr)

CKD-EPI Cys 2012 − CKD-EPI Cr 2021, in mL/min/1.73 m² — the same discordance left unscaled instead of divided by the creatinine estimate. Unlike the percentage version this one is not scale-invariant, so it is taken on the indexed scale, the conventional way to read a difference between two equations. The dashed marker is at 0 (the two equations agree); the −10 % marker of the other panels is a percentage and has no counterpart here.

Code 
emit_plots(lapply(LOESS_EQS, function(eq)
  overlay_plot(cl_nonindex, eq, xvar = "egfr_diff", xlab = DIFF_XLAB, xlim = DIFF_XLIM,
               binw = 5, pct_axis = FALSE, ref_at = 0,
               xscale = tick_x(DIFF_BREAKS, pct = FALSE))),
  "carbo20-sens-absdiff")

<U+2B07><U+FE0F> Download these panels as PowerPoint (editable)

Sensitivity 2 — eGFR % difference against Cockcroft-Gault

100 × (BSA-adjusted eGFRcr-cys − Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance) / Cockcroft-Gault, both terms in absolute mL/min. This is the discordance index the grant figures use, carried over unchanged including its axis window. The dashed marker is at −10 %, as in the primary panels.

Code 
emit_plots(lapply(LOESS_EQS, function(eq)
  overlay_plot(cl_nonindex, eq, xvar = "egfr_pctdiff_cg", xlab = PCTD_CG_XLAB,
               xlim = PCTD_CG_XLIM, binw = BINW, ref_at = REF_LINE,
               xscale = tick_x(PCTD_CG_BREAKS))),
  "carbo20-sens-pctdiffcg")

<U+2B07><U+FE0F> Download these panels as PowerPoint (editable)

NoteReading the two creatinine panels in Sensitivity 2

Sensitivity 2 measures eGFRcr-cys against Cockcroft-Gault, so the Cockcroft-Gault panel and, to a lesser degree, the CKD-EPI Cr-Cys 2021 panel are partly self-referential — the equation being tested also defines the x axis. The same caveat applies to the CKD-EPI Cys 2012 and CKD-EPI Cr 2021 panels in the primary and Sensitivity 1 sets.

ECOG performance status (whole 1,200 cohort)

Code 
emit_plots(lapply(LOESS_EQS, function(eq)
  bar_line_plot(cl_nonindex, eq, "ecog_grp", "ECOG performance status")), "carbo20-ecog")

<U+2B07><U+FE0F> Download these panels as PowerPoint (editable)

Fried frailty classification (592 patients with a Fried class)

Code 
emit_plots(lapply(LOESS_EQS, function(eq)
  bar_line_plot(cl_nonindex, eq, "fried_grp", "Fried frailty class")), "carbo20-fried")

<U+2B07><U+FE0F> Download these panels as PowerPoint (editable)

Muscle Z-score (465 body-composition cohort)

Same construction as the eGFR % difference panels above. No reference line here — the −10 % marker belongs to the eGFR difference and has no counterpart on the Z-score scale.

Code 
emit_plots(lapply(LOESS_EQS, function(eq)
  overlay_plot(cl_nonindex_465, eq, xvar = "muscle_z", xlab = MZ_XLAB, xlim = MZ_XLIM,
               binw = 0.25, pct_axis = FALSE, ref_at = NULL, data = dat_465)),
  "carbo20-musclez")

<U+2B07><U+FE0F> Download these panels as PowerPoint (editable)

15 Final heatmap plots

The manuscript heatmaps. Dosing thresholds come from final_chemos.docx; every other section on this page uses the earlier rules, so these tables supersede them for the drugs listed below. Two drugs are not in that document and keep their existing rules: carboplatin (dosed to a target AUC by the Calvert formula, so it has no threshold table) and cisplatin (this project’s tier rule, unchanged from the earlier sections).

Rows are the seven equations of the manuscript table, in its order and grouping — creatinine-based (including Cockcroft-Gault), then cystatin, then combined — with black rules closing each block. CKD-EPI 4-marker is excluded. Every column header carries its N. Cells are the % of that subgroup over- or under-dosed relative to measured GFR, coloured yellow → red and saturating at 30 %.

ImportantTwo things to read carefully

The sarcopenia columns are a different denominator. Non-sarcopenic (N=308) and Sarcopenic (N=157) come from the 465-patient body-composition subset, not the full 1,200. They sum to 465. Every other column is drawn from the whole cohort.

Tier 0 does not always mean “avoid”. The thresholds are ordinal dose levels. For etoposide the lowest tier is a 50 % dose, and for melphalan it is 140 mg/m². A patient moving into the lowest tier is therefore not always being told to stop the drug.

Dosing rules used here

Drug Full dose Reduced tiers Lowest tier
Carboplatin (±20 % / ±15 %) † Calvert AUC 5 — band rule, not a threshold
Cisplatin † ≥60 50–59 → −25 %; 40–49 → −50 % <40 avoid
Pemetrexed ≥45 — <45 avoid
Etoposide ≥50 15–50 → −25 % <15 → −50 %
Capecitabine ≥50 30–50 → −25 % <30 avoid
Bleomycin ≥60 46–60 → 70 %; 30–45.99 → 60 % <30 avoid
Ifosfamide >60 40–60 → 75 %; 20–40 → 50 % <20 avoid
Melphalan >60 (200 mg/m²) — ≤60 → 140 mg/m²
Methotrexate >60 45–59.99 → −25 %; 30–44.99 → −50 % <30 avoid

† Not from final_chemos.docx — see above.

All GFR units mL/min (non-indexed) or mL/min/1.73 m² (indexed), matched to the reference measured GFR on the same scale.

16 Table 1 — Fried frailty cohort (N = 592)

Baseline characteristics of the 592 patients with a Fried frailty class, stratified by that class. Rows and row order follow the manuscript template. Every variable here is complete in the source file, so there is no missing-data column.

  • Continuous rows — median [IQR], or mean (SD) where the row label says so. Test: Kruskal-Wallis across the three classes.
  • Categorical rows — n (%) within each class. Test: chi-square, or Fisher’s exact (Monte Carlo, 20,000 replicates) when any expected count is below 5. A multi-level variable carries one p-value, on its header row.
WarningThe Fried cohort is not a random subset

Fried assessment had an age ≥ 60 eligibility criterion: 0 of the 595 patients under 60 were assessed, against 97–99 % of those 60 and over. The 592 are therefore older and sicker than the cohort as a whole (mean age 69.1 vs 48.7 years, measured GFR 70.6 vs 91.8 mL/min/1.73 m²). Read this table as describing who was assessed, not as a sample of the 1,200.

ImportantSeven cancer-site labels are still unmapped

site.ajcc has exactly the 11 groups the template lists, but the source file ships no codebook for the codes. Four are fixed beyond doubt by their sex distribution and are labelled: 6 = Breast (272, 98.9 % female), 7 = Female reproductive organs (60, 100 % female), 11 = Male genital organs (262, 0 % female) and 9 = Endocrine system (39, 84.6 % female — thyroid). The remaining seven cannot be told apart from the data alone, so they print as their code:

Code n % female Code n % female
1 109 28.4 % 5 54 46.3 %
2 251 44.6 % 8 82 34.1 %
3 34 41.2 % 10 10 40.0 %
4 27 48.1 %

Give me the mapping and it goes in one place — SITE_LABS in the data chunk.

Two codings were resolved against the data, not assumed. Smoking is not in the intuitive order: checked against the file’s own never./former./current.smoker indicator columns, 1 is Current (128 patients) and 2 is Former (468), with 0 = Never (604). stage = 5 carries stageV for all 55 of its patients (and TIS for 43), which is the unstageable band the template calls Not applicable.

Code 
.t1 <- build_table1()
.t1_ft <- table1_ft(.t1)
save_ft_docx(.t1_ft, "table1_fried592")
cat(flextable::flextable_to_rmd(.t1_ft)); cat("\n\n")

17 Notes

  • Reference. Measured GFR (⁵¹Cr-EDTA) is the gold standard; each equation is compared to mGFR on the matching scale (indexed vs indexed, non-indexed vs non-indexed).
  • Scale. Calvert carboplatin dosing was derived on absolute (non-indexed) GFR, so the non-indexed tables are the clinically conventional view for carboplatin; indexed GFR is the conventional scale for CKD-staging cutoffs.
  • Direction. Creatinine-based equations tend to overdose (they overestimate GFR, especially at low BMI / low muscle mass); cystatin-based equations tend to underdose.
  • Counterfactual. No administered doses exist in this file, so every drug rule is applied to all 1,200 patients to estimate misclassification rates, not actual prescribing errors.
